report:
Reviewed the full owned_products claim, all three implementation associations and both test entries; captured the checking design and accepted stash-ownership RFD. This is source inspection, not a fresh behavioral test execution. No source changes were made.

The requirements are immutable CST input, fresh owned semantic storage for checked signatures and bodies, self-contained Stashed results, and deterministic content-based equality/backdating independent of allocation address and source-tree lifetime. In sig.rs, Check borrows source_stash immutably, constructs target_stash with Stash::new, and finish consumes the checker to move that output stash into Stashed. In finalize.rs, finalize_typed_body creates another fresh target stash, recursively resolves/copies expressions, patterns, type slices, aliases and call targets, allocates locals/root there and returns Stashed::new(target, body). Source storage is borrowed, not mutated by the copy. These paths implement an explicit ownership boundary rather than treating source indices as globally valid handles.

The associated sage-stash implementation stores stash, root and fingerprint together. Stashed::new recursively hashes the root using its owning stash; FingerprintHasher derives child fingerprints from content, with entry indices serving as memoization keys rather than the value's identity. PartialEq compares fingerprints, Hash uses that fingerprint, and salsa::Update returns unchanged for equal Stashed values. Therefore the inspected update boundary uses semantic content fingerprints rather than allocation addresses. The RFD clarifies that compact handles remain stash-local and release builds rely on correct structural copying; this review does not claim that the representation type alone prevents every accidental foreign handle.

The ordinary body_finalization_resolves_types_into_a_fresh_stash test creates an inference variable nested inside a tuple type, unifies it with i32, finalizes an expression, asserts the source entry remains InferVar(0), and traverses the returned output stash to assert the tuple element is i32. It directly establishes that this nested output resolves independently without rewriting the input. It does not drop the source before reading output, traverse every semantic node kind, check signatures, compare recomputation fingerprints, or exercise downstream Salsa reuse.

The checking_owned_products TODO explicitly retains those broad verification prerequisites: structural traversal detecting source-stash or tree-sitter pointers, equal recomputation producing equal fingerprints, and a persistent edit demonstrating that an equal recomputed product stops downstream reexecution. It has no assertions and remains a visible deferral, not proof. Completing that ownership/fingerprint/backdating matrix is required before treating the full claim as exhaustively verified. All associated implementations and tests and all claim components are accounted for; no concrete additional defect was identified in these inspected paths and no edits are requested.
